proposed_connector.name: edgar_xbrl.company_facts_ratio
proposed_connector.description: Pulls SEC EDGAR Company Facts XBRL for a CIK and derives the PFIC-test diagnostics: passive-income ratio (interest/investment income / total gross income) and passive-asset ratio (cash + marketable securities / total assets) by fiscal year. A reported >=75% passive-income share or >=50% passive-asset share corroborates the issuer's PFIC self-classification.
proposed_connector.sample_invocation: GET https://data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyfacts/CIK0001453015.json -> extract us-gaap:InterestIncomeOperating, us-gaap:Revenues, us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue, us-gaap:MarketableSecuritiesCurrent, us-gaap:Assets; compute passive_income_pct and passive_asset_pct per FY
proposed_connector.rationale: Ballard's PFIC self-classification is economically equivalent to asserting that its operating revenue is dwarfed by interest on cash / securities, OR that >=50% of assets are cash/marketable securities. SEC Company Facts XBRL exposes both numerators and denominators, so the assertion is structurally adjudicatable via PFIC-test arithmetic on the issuer's own audited financials — but no existing catalog connector exposes Company Facts XBRL.
proposed_connector.completeness: All SEC XBRL filers (10-K, 20-F, 40-F that include US-GAAP or IFRS tagging).

claims.extraction_notes: PFIC self-classification is a structural distress signal for a cohort that should be operating: a company with material fuel-cell revenue can't normally pass the 75% passive-income test. Adjudicating this from public XBRL (passive income vs total gross income; cash+marketable securities vs total assets) corroborates whether operating revenue has collapsed enough for PFIC status to be plausible. No catalog connector exposes XBRL company facts.
